nodes.label: Privilege Guest Program
nodes.rationale: An existing invitation-only hotel benefits programme at Steigenberger Doha run on printed letters and plastic cards; digitised because the member loses the paper sheet and the hotel has no data at all about usage.

nodes.label: Fixed Benefit Discount Schedule
nodes.rationale: Five categories (F&B 25%, Rooms 30%, Spa 40%, Meetings 25%, Lifestyle 30%) with party-size caps. A fixed discount schedule, deliberately not a points currency.

nodes.label: No Points, Tiers or Balances
nodes.rationale: Version 1 assumed a multi-brand coalition with a points currency; the client narrowed scope twice. Nothing is earned, benefits are granted on joining, and one membership level means every member sees the same schedule. The schema comment states that a balance column appearing would be a misreading of the specification.

nodes.label: Member Guest App
nodes.rationale: Phone-first, public internet, seven screens: Activate, Sign in/Verify, Offers, Offer detail, Profile, Card.

nodes.label: Administrator Panel
nodes.rationale: Desktop, hotel-network only, six sections: Members, Requests, Redemptions, Benefits, Reports, Administrators.

nodes.label: Digital Card Without QR Credential
nodes.rationale: Earlier drafts specified a scannable rotating credential plus a counter-staff verification page. Version 3 removed both: a 40% spa discount is worth stealing, so a self-declared or screenshot-forwardable credential would be worth forging. Entitlement is established by a named administrator deciding a request, never by software trusting a presented code.

nodes.label: Single Administrator Account Type
nodes.rationale: Manager, support and outlet-staff roles from version 2 were removed. Only named Administrator accounts can sign in; legacy role values survive purely so historical records keep naming whoever acted, and are forced suspended by a database CHECK.

nodes.label: Caddy Edge Proxy
nodes.rationale: Automatic TLS, HSTS, CSP, serves both apps and proxies the API. Refuses /admin/* from outside the hotel network on the API path itself, not merely on the panel's hostname — the UI is not the control.

nodes.label: Fastify API
nodes.rationale: One Fastify 5 process on Node 20 serving both surfaces. Route-level config hooks make deny-by-default enforceable at startup; Zod rejects unknown fields rather than ignoring them.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL 16 Authoritative Store
nodes.rationale: Chosen for exact decimal money, table-level privilege revocation and CHECK constraints. Never exposed to the host or the internet.

nodes.label: Google Sheets Mirror
nodes.rationale: Optional, one-way, off by default hotel-facing export. Carries membership numbers, usage counts and benefit configuration; deliberately excludes names, phones, emails, request notes, consents and audit records. A standing bulk disclosure that should be an explicit client decision.

nodes.label: Invitation and Activation Flow
nodes.rationale: Onboarding runs backwards from a normal app: the hotel creates the account and the member claims it. 160-bit single-use code shown once and stored only as a hash; consumed inside the same transaction that activates the membership so two simultaneous attempts cannot both succeed. Reusable codes would let anyone holding a discarded letter join.

nodes.label: Member OTP Sign-in
nodes.rationale: Phone number then a six-digit passcode valid five minutes, five attempts. No password ever exists for a member, so none can be reused from another breach.

nodes.label: Administrator Password + TOTP Sign-in
nodes.rationale: Argon2id password screened against Have I Been Pwned, then a short-lived challenge (not a session), then a TOTP code. First sign-in forces enrolment; ten recovery codes shown once. An emailed code would not be a second factor.

nodes.label: Request, Decide, Record Loop
nodes.rationale: The flow the product exists for: a member never grants themselves anything. Pending, then approved or declined by a named administrator, then fulfilled by a separate redemption row. Enforced: one open request per benefit, one decision, one approval spent at most once (unique constraint), party-size caps checked at recording.

nodes.label: Rate Snapshot on Redemption
nodes.rationale: The discount percentage in force is copied onto the redemption row and never read back from the benefit. Changing dining from 25% to 20% changes tomorrow's offer without rewriting last month's record or restating a report already sent.

nodes.label: Redemption Immutability
nodes.rationale: Redemptions cannot be edited or deleted — not by policy but because UPDATE and DELETE are revoked at the database level. A correction is a new reversing row with a negated amount pointing at the original, so totals net correctly without any query knowing about reversals. Idempotency keys stop a retried submission creating a second row.

nodes.label: Database Role Split (owner vs app)
nodes.rationale: The application connects as a role that is not the schema owner; migrations run as the owner over a separate connection so the revocation cannot be undone by the migration that creates the tables. An owner cannot be denied access to its own tables, so immutability only means something because the application is not the owner.

nodes.label: Deny-by-Default Route Authorisation
nodes.rationale: Every route must declare its required permission; an undeclared route prevents the server from booting rather than failing at runtime with a 403. A wrapper you must remember to call is exactly the control that fails under deadline. Public endpoints must say 'public' explicitly, so the opt-out is greppable.

nodes.label: Query Scoping in the WHERE Clause
nodes.rationale: Records are filtered in the database WHERE clause, never fetched then checked — fetch-then-check leaks existence through timing and error shape even when the response is a 404. The scope combinator uses AND rather than an object spread, because a spread would let a member's own identifier overwrite the one asked about. Held by fetch-then-check.test.ts.

nodes.label: Confidentiality of the Membership List
nodes.rationale: The membership list is the asset. The reference card is issued to a member of the Qatari ruling family; the list is a record of named prominent individuals and their movements. Treated as the primary design constraint rather than a later addition, which is why controls go beyond what a loyalty app would normally carry.

nodes.label: Small-Cohort Suppression
nodes.rationale: Any figure backed by fewer than five distinct members returns 'insufficient data'. The cohort size itself is withheld, since publishing '3 members' is the same disclosure stated outright.

nodes.label: Two-Layer Log Redaction
nodes.rationale: The logger redacts known paths and a serialiser walks whatever it is handed removing anything named like personal data at any depth. Two mechanisms because either alone leaves a gap; the second is what makes an accidental 'log the whole member object' call safe.

nodes.label: Two-Audience Token Separation
nodes.rationale: A member token is rejected by an administrator endpoint at the audience check before it is inspected. Algorithm pinned to a fixed allowlist so alg:none and confusion attacks fail before the signature is examined.

nodes.label: Refresh Token Rotation with Reuse Detection
nodes.rationale: Refresh tokens are single-use and grouped into families; presenting a spent one revokes the whole family, because a legitimate client never replays one. Stored in an httpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict cookie scoped to one endpoint; a test strips comments from every client source and asserts no localStorage, sessionStorage or document.cookie use.

nodes.label: Benefit Versioning and Attribution
nodes.rationale: The programme materials state benefits may change without notice, which made editability the most important configuration requirement: every value a member sees is a database row, never a constant. Each edit increments a version and records who made it.

nodes.label: Reporting and CSV Export
nodes.rationale: Usage by month, benefit and outlet; dormant members and members issued a card who never activated. Export carries membership numbers rather than names, is a separate permission capped at five per administrator per day, and every attempt is recorded.

nodes.label: Eleven-Table Data Model
nodes.rationale: Member, ClaimCode, StaffUser, Benefit, BenefitRequest, Redemption, ConsentRecord, AuditLog, RefreshToken, OtpCode, MfaRecoveryCode. Constraints carry as much of the design as the application code. Money stored as integer minor units (fils), never floating point.

nodes.label: Append-Only Audit Trail
nodes.rationale: Thirty-eight distinct actions including every member record viewed, every export, every authorisation denial and every refresh-token replay. Metadata carries membership numbers, never names; a failed sign-in against a non-existent account deliberately does not record the email tried, or the attacker's guesses would be written into the trail.

nodes.label: Account Enumeration and Timing Resistance
nodes.rationale: Passcode requests return the same response whether or not the number belongs to a member; a sign-in against a non-existent account still runs a full Argon2 verification against a dummy hash; unknown, expired, used and wrong-phone invitation codes all return one identical message.

nodes.label: Health Data Excluded by Construction
nodes.rationale: Spa treatment records can imply health information, so the redemption table has no column for a treatment or description and no endpoint accepts one — only that a spa benefit was used.

nodes.label: Finding: Stale VERIFICATION_SESSION_HMAC_SECRET
nodes.rationale: Reported as blocking a production start: docker-compose.prod.yml was said to still require a secret belonging to the removed verification page. The file as it now stands sets VERIFICATION_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS instead and contains no such mandatory secret, so this finding appears already resolved.

nodes.label: Finding: 25 Failing Tests, One Cause
nodes.rationale: 344 of 369 tests pass. All 25 failures trace to one guard refusing member creation without an email while passcodes are delivered by email; two older test files create members without one and cascade. No product code is wrong, but a red suite hides the next real regression.

nodes.label: Finding: SECURITY-REVIEW.md Documentation Drift
nodes.rationale: Lists secure cookies as deferred though implemented, states no security headers are configured though the edge sets a full policy, and refers throughout to three client applications and a verification page that no longer exist.

nodes.label: Pre-Launch Blockers
nodes.rationale: Green the suite and remove the stale secret; settle passcode delivery (SMS unprovisioned, email interim); hosting region and a Qatari data protection impact assessment (fine up to QAR 1,000,000 on its own); alerting; key management and rotation; an anonymisation endpoint; approve or drop the Sheets mirror.
